title: Let deleted articles be restored
hints: Before writing code, list every place in src/store that reads articles or comments. Each one needs a decision about deleted articles.
If most of the app should behave as if a deleted article is gone, make that the default, and add a separate way to see it for the few places that must.
Keep the deleted slugs in a Set next to the articles rather than adding a field to each article. Then responses keep their shape on their own, and the slug check can still see every article.

hiddenTestRules.deleting > hides the article from the li: A deleted article is gone from GET /articles and from GET /authors/:author/articles.
hiddenTestRules.deleting > hides the article from its au: A deleted article is gone from GET /articles and from GET /authors/:author/articles.
hiddenTestRules.deleting > answers 404 on every route fo: Every other route for a deleted article is 404 with { error: 'Article not found' }, including its comments, PATCH and a second DELETE.
hiddenTestRules.deleting > leaves the article and its co: GET /stats counts neither the deleted article nor its comments.
hiddenTestRules.deleting > keeps the slug taken: A deleted article's slug stays taken: POST /articles with it is 409, as for any other article, so it can always be restored.
hiddenTestRules.restoring > brings the article back exac: POST /articles/:slug/restore brings a deleted article back, and answers 200 with the article.
hiddenTestRules.restoring > brings the comments back and: Its comments come back too, but the response is the article only, with no comments.
hiddenTestRules.restoring > answers 404 for an article t: Restoring an article that doesn't exist is 404 with { error: 'Article not found' }.
hiddenTestRules.restoring > answers 409 for an article t: Restoring an article that isn't deleted is 409 with { error: 'Article is not deleted' }.
hiddenTestRules.shape > adds no new fields to any respon: Articles in responses have the same fields as today: nothing new, whether or not they were ever deleted.
